Hong Kong C&SD Historical Monitor

Ten sections, each plotted as a local infographic.

Every chart on this page is rendered locally into inline SVG during the build step. Each section leads with the longest available historical series and then adds smaller supporting visuals for context.

Analyses10
Latest source date2026-03-26
Built at2026-03-28 14:16 UTC
Scope

The report uses official Hong Kong Census and Statistics Department web-table metadata and backing CSV files. The raw cache is local, the rendering is local, and rerunning the build will fold in any newly released values for the configured tables.

Update check

No source-date changes were detected in the configured table set during this run.

Section 01

Population level

Primary history: Population

2025 Year-end: 7,510.8 thousand

Year-end population moved from 3,195.3 thousand in 1961 Year-end to 7,510.8 thousand in 2025 Year-end. The historical peak was 7,527.9 thousand in 2023 Year-end.

Year-end population, both sexes, all ages. Event lines mark major external shocks where they fall within the time range.

Section 02

Population growth components

Primary history: Population growth

2025 Year-end: growth 10.2 thousand, net movement 29.1 thousand

Population growth peaked at 254.8 thousand in 1979 Year-end. In the latest year, births were 31.1 thousand and deaths were 50.0 thousand.

Annual year-end population growth history. Event lines provide timing context for shocks and recoveries.

Coverage 1961 Year-end to 2025 Year-end

Latest drivers

Source 110-01003 Population Growth by Component

Official C&SD web table. Last modified on 2026-02-12.

Commentary

Natural increase has weakened over time, so swings in net movement now have a much larger influence on the headline growth result.

Section 03

Ageing and dependency

Primary history: Median age

2025: median age 49.4, dependency ratio 535.0

Median age rose by 22.7 years over the series, while the total dependency ratio increased from 455.0 to 535.0.

Annual population ageing indicators, excluding foreign domestic helpers. Event lines matter less here because the shift is structural rather than cyclical.

Coverage 1982 to 2025
Latest 49.4
Change 85.0%
Peak 49.4 | 2025

Source 110-01004 Dependency ratio and median age of population

Official C&SD web table. Last modified on 2026-03-26.

Commentary

The ageing story is persistent across shocks: short crises interrupt economic series, but they do not reverse the demographic direction of travel.

Section 04

Fertility pressure

Primary history: Total fertility rate

2025: TFR 734.00, crude birth rate 4.1 per 1,000

Total fertility fell from a peak of 3,459.00 in 1971 to 734.00 in the latest release.

Annual fertility indicators. Event lines are included for orientation, but the dominant pattern is the long-run downtrend.

Commentary

The fertility decline is much larger than any temporary rebound, which is why the ageing and household sections reinforce this one.

Section 07

Labour force participation

Primary history: Labour force participation rate

2025: participation 57.0%, labour force 3,811.3 thousand

Participation peaked at 65.1% in 1986 and now sits at 57.0%.

Annual averages for both sexes. The participation rate is the cleaner structural signal, while labour force size is kept as a supporting graphic.

Commentary

A large labour-force headcount does not fully offset a softer participation rate, which is why ageing pressure matters for labour supply.

Commentary

Unlike ageing or fertility, unemployment is sharply cyclical. The event markers matter here because labour-market stress tends to cluster around shocks.
